    Docs/Connector.sln/Connector.Infrastructure/src-Connector.Infrastructure-DataSources-MariaDb
    Module

    src/Connector.Infrastructure/DataSources/MariaDb

    Layer infrastructure · project Connector.Infrastructure

    Project navigation: Connector.Infrastructure

    Overview 🤖

    Manages MariaDB data source connections and queries.

    Responsibilities. Provides connection factory and data source provider for MariaDB, handling connection management, query compilation, and schema reading.

    AI draft from the facts on this page; review it, then write the module's documentation yourself.

    Key components

    Component Kind Used by Summary
    MariaDbDialect class 2 ISqlDialect for MariaDB — every MariaDB-specific fragment the generic query builders emit: backtick identifier quoting, @pN parameter placeholders (MySqlConnector's named-parameter syntax), LIMIT n, CAST(… AS CHAR), <=>, GROUP_CONCAT, and how a value in MariaDbDataSourceProvider's native text format maps to JSON. Stateless; use Instance.
    CompiledMariaDbQuery record 1 A SourceQuery compiled to MariaDB: SQL text plus the @p0, @p1, … parameters it references.
    MariaDbConnectionFactory class 1 Builds and opens MySqlConnections for a MariaDb``DataSourceConfig. Every field is set as a typed builder property, never interpolated into the connection-string text, so no value (e.g. a password containing ;Server=evil) can add or override a key — the same rule as PostgreSqlDataSourceProvider.BuildConnectionString.
    MariaDbQueryCompiler class 1 Compiles the database-neutral SourceQuery into MariaDB SQL — the MariaDB counterpart of PostgreSqlQueryCompiler, with the same guarantees: validated against the given SourceSchema first (SourceQueryValidator), so every emitted identifier is one the schema reported (backtick-quoted by MariaDbDialect); synthetic table aliases (t0, t1, …); every filter value a bound parameter; Limit an Int32 rendered by the dialect.
    MariaDbSchemaReader class 1 Reads the tables of the connection's current database (DATABASE()) from information_schema (TABLES, COLUMNS, KEY_COLUMN_USAGE, REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS) into the same SourceTable shape the PostgreSQL provider returns.
    MariaDbDataSourceProvider class 0 The IDataSourceProvider for MariaDb, over MySqlConnector — the same contract as PostgreSqlDataSourceProvider: connection test and schema read (MariaDbSchemaReader), neutral queries (MariaDbQueryCompiler) and native SQL the export builders render with MariaDbDialect. Stateless singleton; every call opens and disposes its own connection (MariaDbConnectionFactory).

    Member Summary Derived from code Complexity
    OpenConnectionAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) An open ADO.NET connection for callers that need more than one query per call — the import path's multi-statement transaction. The caller disposes it. 1
    ValidateConfig(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) Whether config has what this provider needs to connect (required fields, a valid TLS mode or instance URL): a user-facing message, or null when it's usable. Checked before any connection attempt; the only place per-source-type config rules live. 1
    TargetHost(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) The host a connection with the (validated) config reaches — what the SSRF check in POST /api/connection resolves. 1
    IsAlwaysEncrypted(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) True when config can only ever reach the source encrypted — never falling back to plaintext. 1
    TestConnectionAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Never throws for a reachability/credential failure — reported, sanitized, via Failed instead. 2
    ReadSchemaAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Reads the live schema (tables/columns/PK/FK) of the data source described by config. Throws on failure — unlike TestConnectionAsync, this is called once a connection is already known-good and a failure here is a real, reportable error. 1
    ExecuteAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceQuery, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Compiles against the live schema (read fresh, so a dropped column fails as InvalidSourceQueryException before any SQL runs) and executes. 1
    ExecuteNativeAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Executes caller-built, provider-native SQL as-is and returns its rows generically — the path DynamicExportService's JSON-tree builders still use for what SourceQuery cannot express yet (knowledge/architecture/source-query-model.md §5). Same error contract as ExecuteAsync, minus schema validation. 4

    Member Summary Derived from code Complexity
    QuoteIdentifier(string) Quotes a table/column/alias name so it is always read as an identifier, never as syntax. 1
    BuildParameterName(int) The placeholder for the index-th bound parameter, as it appears in SQL text. Also a valid parameter name for the matching driver's parameter collection. 1
    BuildLimit(int) The clause appended to a SELECT to cap its row count at limit. 1
    QuoteStringLiteral(string) A string literal holding value verbatim — for constant text that has to be part of the statement itself (a JSON object key, an aggregation delimiter) rather than a parameter. 1
    CastToText(string) Converts expression to text, so it can be compared with a text value or emitted as text regardless of the column's own type. 1
    BuildNullSafeEquals(string, string) A null-safe equality test: true when both sides are equal or both are null. 1
    BuildMatchesAny(string, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string>, System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary<string, object?>) True when expression equals any of values — how the export tree engine fetches every child row of a whole level in one query instead of one query per parent. Binds the values into parameters (named from BuildParameterName, continuing at its current count) in whatever shape the backend needs: one array parameter, or one parameter per value. 2
    ConvertNativeTextToJson(string, string) Maps a value in MariaDbDataSourceProvider's native text format (see its FormatNative) to the JSON value PostgreSQL's to_json gives the equivalent column, so a nested export is the same document against either backend: numeric types → JSON numbers with the same digits, BOOL (TINYINT(1)) → true/false, JSON → embedded, DATETIME/TIMESTAMP → ISO 8601 with a T, everything else → a string. 7
    FormatValue(object, string) The connector's string form of a non-null column value as the driver returned it, for a column the backend calls dataType: date/timestamp columns as yyyy-MM-dd, everything else the value's own ToString(). Shared by the provider's row materialization and the import walker, so old values read for a diff match exported values exactly. 4
    BuildStringAggregate(string, string) Aggregates expression (as text) over the rows of the enclosing SELECT into one string joined by delimiter; null values are skipped. 1
    BuildSetClause(string, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string>, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string?>, System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary<string, object?>) The SET clause (without the keyword) of an UPDATE on table that assigns each of columns the matching text value in values, converted by the backend to the column's own type. Binds the values into parameters (named from BuildParameterName, continuing at its current count). Used by the import releaser's updates. 2
    BuildInsertRow(string, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string>, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string?>, System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary<string, object?>) An INSERT of one row into table, setting each of columns to the matching text value in values, converted by the backend to the column's own type (uuid, date, number…). Binds the values into parameters (named from BuildParameterName, continuing at its current count). Used by the import releaser's root-row inserts. 2
